module.label: Scenes & lobbies
module.description: Chooses gameplay or a conversation view.

flows.label: Game starts
flows.detail: Game connection queues a manual-revision-scoped intent. The bounded feature loop cancels its older return and asks SceneDirector for gameplay. Newer deliberate choices reject stale work; a temporary owner defers accepted automatic intent. Streamer automatic holds also defer the gameplay request. The feature lifetime owns one SessionControls hold and releases it without applying deferred work on shutdown.

manual.text: If this intent was captured before your scene choice, it is stale and cannot overwrite that choice. A genuinely new trigger may create new intent.

flows.label: Game ends
flows.detail: Game disconnect records the shared hold and queues a manual-revision-scoped intent. A registered enabled client provider owns automatic lobbies; otherwise the switcher waits for the hold, chooses a rotation location inside SceneDirector preparation and hides the shared desktop. Deferred requests retain the revision guard. Shutdown withdraws only this ownerÃ¢â‚¬â„¢s pending intent. The accepted lobby is repaired from the complete published layer snapshot before it appears. Each chat browser has its own board dimensions; the existing camera and desktop resources are reused. Break and Wrap up retain their automatic hold through newer game events; Auto scenes can resume the latest valid request. The feature releases only its own hold without switching scenes during shutdown.

flows.label: Choose a scene or lobby
flows.detail: Gallery, desk and voice choices prepare the selected world before SceneDirector shows it. SessionControls owns Break/Wrap up intent under an identity-scoped automatic hold. Failed selection rolls back only a newly acquired hold; successful Lobby/Game selection or shutdown releases without resuming deferred intent. Auto scenes releases with resume. Desk lobby entry hides desktop capture. Other entries retain their visibility policy. Worlds outside rotation remain selectable. Newer choices during inventory reads reject stale selection before repair. Native entries use the shared observer; saved group choices resolve to their parent. The offline catalog exposes authored previews without OBS. Saved shuffle/fixed selection belongs to this feature; fixed selection preserves rotation membership and layouts, while shuffle excludes the currently visible candidate when alternatives exist. Inventory publishes the choice and layouts from one settings snapshot. Explicit manual selections can override the current view without replacing future rotation preferences. Next lobby excludes the current world when alternatives exist without changing saved fixed/shuffle preferences. The public opening handoff checks the supplied manual revision before preparation. Other scenes exposes only installed named presentation destinations.

flows.label: Native lobby passage
flows.detail: The finite off-air installer adds only the featureÃ¢â‚¬â„¢s OBS script entry. OBS owns one frontend subscription, native show/hide transitions and style/duration controls, with no timer, socket or Hub worker. Show/hide pairs use the same mask and duration. Existing personal item transitions take priority. Unload releases its callback and removes only its own named item transitions. No camera, chat, filters, transforms, global transition or output path is changed.

steps.label: Preserve collection and personal controls
steps.detail: Snapshot before a finite inactive-collection update. Verify the selected filename/name; duplicate names require the observed filename.

steps.label: Install native location handoffs
steps.detail: Only add the OBS script entry; preserve other scripts and personal style/duration on repeated installs.

steps.label: Animate complete lobby layers
steps.detail: OBS show/hide transition instances follow scene-item visibility chosen by existing scene routing.

flows.label: Prepare the chosen lobby
flows.detail: The feature publishes complete per-world source and placement data. Shared mechanics resolve required resources, snapshot before the first repair, and update only named layers when their settings, visibility, placement or relative stacking differ. The publication/presentation lock keeps a saved edit from racing an older layout. Image settings, nested camera filters, personal CSS and unowned overlays survive; only active chat browsers remain loaded. Deferred and stale scene intents do not repair anything until accepted. Ready worlds optionally publish a transparent living-world layer after its original foreground (or camera for a flat painting) and before dedicated chat, with all three saved live apertures passed explicitly. Other worlds retain their authored layers. Locations may be groups in the single Lobbies scene. Enumeration uses the group transport; missing group children reject before mutation and require offline structural repair.

steps.label: Resolve camera, screen and owned layers

effects.protection: SceneDirector admission precedes all preparation. Shared mechanical layer writes cannot select the program scene or edit nested camera/device settings.

flows.label: A lobby becomes a living world

trigger.label: A ready living lobby is visible

flows.detail: The original OBS painting stays beneath a world layer. Five selected worlds can paint versioned replacement artwork through that existing layer; saved live apertures are still cleared after the complete painting and every accent. The other worlds retain their original painted overlays. Feature-local chaos-cast assembles finite setup/payoff jokes, chaos-ink owns illustrated game props, and lobby-cameos adds painted-character performances through the public PaintedWorld.drawVisitor contract. LobbyResidents owns three decoded connected-alpha sprite caches per redesigned world, continuous room routines and perch handoff during cameos; late decode and teardown release the same presentation resources. Afterparty is independent and unchanged. Eleven ready worlds (Reef, Forge, Sanctuary, Sky Harbor, Storm Coast, Phoenix Observatory, Spirit Railway, Tavern, Future Lounge, Spirit Arcade and Aurora Camp) each supply their own painted landmark motion, ambience and finite themed guests. New invitations retain existing instances, automatic entrances use novelty and soft pressure, and switching the studio world replaces its single document while rejecting stale selections. Complete saved desktop, camera and chat rectangles are cleared after all accents. Hidden documents pause; native OBS unloads inactive sources; teardown releases clocks, instances and cached canvases. Finite off-air installation preserves original inputs, filters, transforms and the program scene. No audio, new Hub worker, socket or program-scene writer is introduced. Maintenance reruns enumerate installed groups and reject missing group children before any installation writes. Manual cues use the existing Hub SSE channel only in a visible native world document; private previews never subscribe. Cue age, world identity and bounded deduplication guard dispatch; hide/page exit closes the subscription. Living-world browser sources explicitly enable OBS custom FPS so the authored 24 FPS source limit is honored independently of the 60 FPS stream. The finite frame-cap repair changes only the missing flag on matching existing sources, with rollback settings snapshots and off-air checks. Feature-owned saved apertures are passed as optional destination occlusions. PaintedPatch skips only triangles whose current deformed bounds lie fully within a later-cleared aperture, including a conservative antialias/seam margin. Each frame rechecks geometry, preserving re-entry, pixel output, mesh density and custom placement.

steps.label: Publish saved live apertures
steps.detail: Optional layer data comes from motion.layer and presentation.plan; original Base and any Foreground remain image sources.

steps.label: Cache painting and plan finite entrances
steps.detail: Public mechanics take feature-provided deformation and cue data; plan history and instances remain bounded.

steps.label: Animate the world and its visitors
steps.detail: Feature artists own palette, physical occlusion, landmark motion and guest performances on one document clock. Selected worlds load versioned art into the same decoded-art owner; full-plate rendering precedes cached deformation, continuous painted residents and finite comic visitors. Three resident caches preserve alpha silhouettes; a resident leaves its perch while participating in a larger performance.

steps.label: Keep live display areas clear
steps.detail: Draw the native OBS layer directly into its output canvas and clear complete saved rectangles after every accent. Only optional previews allocate a second full-frame surface to paint empty artwork behind the transparent layer.

steps.label: Pause or release document resources
steps.detail: Hidden documents suspend drawing; OBS shutdown and pagehide release clocks, guests and canvases.

flows.label: Trigger a current-lobby effect
flows.detail: The feature validates the action against metadata exported from actual authored worlds, checks the current OBS lobby and its installed living layer, then returns a world-scoped cue to the HTTP adapter. The adapter broadcasts through the existing Hub updates owner. Native documents reject stale, wrong-world and repeated cues before handing off to the same artist. Hidden documents and page exit release subscriptions; Afterparty retains its separate public action API. No playback worker or program-scene write is added. The SSE subscription requests only living_lobby_action; Hub status payloads are not sent to animation documents.
